description:
We are a team of four Year 13 students, united by our curiosity about science, innovation, and a shared passion for our planet.

We believe understanding our planet is the first step towards protecting its future. Together, we aim to make environmental information accessible and meaningful, turning complex data into insights that everyone can explore.
summary:
EarthSignal – Environmental Change Across the Arabian Peninsula (2000–2025)

EarthSignal is an interactive research platform investigating how atmospheric and land-surface conditions across the Arabian Peninsula have changed between 2000 and 2025, and how they correlate with each other. Our team processed four NASA MERRA-2 data collections, each providing 312 months of data from January 2000 to December 2025, and used the data to analyse nine environmental variables across five regions. We developed an interactive website featuring maps, time-series graphs, regional comparisons and statistical analysis. Our findings show that temperatures increased by 0.239°C per decade, with the strongest warming in the Northwest (+0.369°C). Root-zone and topsoil wetness also increased. Wind speed was positively associated with dust concentration (r = 0.382), while precipitation was positively associated with soil wetness (r = 0.556–0.658). However, overall dust concentrations showed no statistically significant long-term trend. EarthSignal combines interactive visualisations with linear regression, Mann–Kendall tests, Sen's slope and correlation analysis to identify environmental trends and assess their significance. Our aim is to make complex NASA data easier to explore and understand, helping users see where environmental changes are happening, how significant they are and how different conditions relate to one another.
details:
🌍 EarthSignal is an interactive platform that explores how environmental conditions across the Arabian Peninsula have changed between 2000 and 2025, particularly in relation to dust activity.

🔬 Our project uses NASA's MERRA-2 data to investigate nine environmental variables, including temperature, humidity, wind speed, precipitation, soil wetness and dust concentration. We collected and processed data files for 312 months from four NASA datasets using Python. We divided the Arabian Peninsula into five regions so that we could compare how environmental conditions have changed in different areas.

💻 We then developed a website where users can explore these changes through maps, graphs, regional comparisons and statistical results. To make sure our findings were meaningful, we used methods such as linear regression, Mann–Kendall tests and correlation analysis to identify trends and examine relationships between variables.

📊 One of our key findings was that temperatures across the study area increased by approximately 0.239°C per decade. We also found that wind speed was positively associated with dust concentration, although dust levels did not show a statistically significant overall long-term trend.

🌱 What makes EarthSignal different is that it does not look at environmental variables separately. It brings together atmospheric and land-surface conditions to help users explore how they relate to one another. Throughout the project, we considered regional differences, seasonal changes, data quality and the statistical significance of our results.

We hope EarthSignal makes NASA's environmental data easier to understand and allows more people to explore the changes taking place across the Arabian Peninsula, rather than simply reading about them.
